title: Expire-and-regenerate pages: let cells decay, recompute on miss
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: disable refresh entirely; each DRAM page carries a write timestamp, and any page older than its guaranteed retention counts as discarded, so reading it traps to the runtime, which regenerates the data from source (re-decompress weights from flash, recompute activations from checkpoints, refetch KV from a cheaper tier).
why: Zero refresh power; because regeneration is rare for hot data, the fab can target ~10 ms retention instead of 64 ms, cutting required Cs ~3x and with it capacitor height, etch time and support masks (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Datacenter fleets as ore: reverse-fab reclaim of retired DRAM dies
idea: Scale shift from fab to fleet: DIMMs retired after 4-6 years are laser/chemically decapped, dies are retested and rebinned, then re-assembled onto new substrates or CXL expander cards as capacity-tier memory with stronger ECC.
why: Adds bits with ~zero fab capex; a hyperscaler fleet could recover 30-60% of retired bits at <20% of new-die cost.

title: Origami artist: roll one flat DRAM membrane into twenty tiers
idea: An origami artist turns a flat sheet into volume. Pattern one 2D cell array on a strained bilayer nanomembrane (e.g., SiN/SiGe) over a sacrificial layer; on release, built-in strain rolls it into a tight Swiss roll of ~20 turns, so one 2D lithography pass yields 20 tiers, with wordlines running along the roll and contacted at its edge.
why: Gets 3D density (fact 2) from 2D lithography, avoiding 26-tier stack deposition and deep etch; litho cost per bit falls ~1/N with N turns. Speculative: turn-to-turn registration, heat removal, edge contacts.
note: 20 tiers from one 2D pass; turn registration, edge contacts and heat removal are unsolved.

title: Airbnb for idle cleanroom tools: memory prototyping by the hour
idea: Borrowed from Airbnb monetizing spare rooms: a 10-person team builds a booking, recipe-transfer and wafer-logistics platform over idle tool hours in U.S. university, national-lab and 200 mm commercial cleanrooms, so memory startups route split lots across ALD at one site, etch at another and test at a third.
why: Capital and time: a new cell concept today needs a ~$50M pilot line; renting tool hours gives 10-50x cheaper, faster learning cycles on U.S. soil.

title: Matrix Semiconductor's 3D antifuse stack made rewritable with selector-charged capacitors
idea: Matrix Semiconductor's 3D poly-diode antifuse memory (bought by SanDisk in 2005) stacked cheaply at ~4 masks per layer but died for being write-once. Keep the stacked poly pillar process and swap the antifuse for a small planar MIM capacitor charged through a bidirectional punch-through n-p-n selector, giving 1S1C dynamic cells with unlimited endurance, refreshed like DRAM.
why: Meets 100x: no access transistor, no high-AR capacitor, 8-16 DUV decks; est. ~$0.1/GB. Trades: selector leakage forces ms-scale refresh, higher refresh power, thin sense margin.
note: No transistor per bit, ~$0.1/GB; poly punch-through selector leakage and half-select disturb likely kill retention.

title: Thermophoretic wafer shielding allows ISO-7 cleanrooms for DRAM fabs
idea: Effect: thermophoresis. Every exposed wafer is held 10-20 K warmer than the gas around it inside sealed carriers and tool mini-environments; the thermophoretic force pushes sub-100 nm particles away from the warm surface, cutting deposition velocity by more than 100x, so the ballroom can be ISO 7 instead of ISO 3-4.
why: Capital: cleanroom and facilities are ~20-30% of a $15B fab and a large energy load; a cheaper shell could save billions and about a year of U.S. fab construction.

title: Octopus arm ganglia: in-tier decoders built in the same channel film
idea: Octopus arms carry their own ganglia; in a 3D stack, form a small oxide-TFT decoder in each tier from the same channel film and the same slit/hole patterning as the cells, so each tier needs only ~log2(N) shared address lines instead of N individually contacted wordlines.
why: Per-tier contacts, staircases and CMOS drivers stop growing with tier count, so 120+ tiers (~10x bits/mm2) can be built without the periphery (49% of the die) and contact cost scaling up (facts 2, 7).
note: Shared-film decoders per tier cut wordline contacts to log2(N); doubt: decoder TFT quality from lateral cell patterning.

title: Substitute die-to-wafer bonding with micro-transfer-printed DRAM tiles on compute
idea: Release 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM tiles from their wafer by undercutting a sacrificial layer, pick thousands at once with an elastomer stamp, and print them directly over compute tiles on the processor wafer, followed by planarization and a via step for um-scale connections.
why: Constraint: tiles ~5 um above cores give ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit access (>=10x below HBM); capital: stamps place thousands of tiles per cycle with no hybrid-bond aligner or TSVs, and tiles can come from older fabs.

title: 1970s CCD memory flipped vertical inside a 3D NAND stack
idea: CCD memories (Intel 2416, Fairchild) died because serial shifting lost to DRAM's random access. Turn a 3D NAND stack into vertical CCD shift registers: 2-phase clock its 300 word-line layers to push 4-level charge packets along an IGZO channel whose low generation current preserves packets for seconds, with one sense amp per string top and no storage transistor or capacitor per bit.
why: Meets 100x: NAND fab cost structure with no per-bit device, 2 bits per packet; est. ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades: ~150 ns average shift latency for random words, best for streamed AI weights and KV pages.
note: No per-bit device on NAND cost base; doubt is charge-transfer efficiency over hundreds of IGZO stages and serial latency.

title: Vertical CCD strings in a 3D-NAND stack, four phase contacts
idea: Revive 1970s CCD serial memory (Fairchild F464, Intel 2416), which needed no contact or access transistor per bit, as vertical charge-coupled strings: a 3D-NAND-style alternating oxide/gate stack is etched once for channel holes, and every fourth gate layer is tied to the same clock phase so charge packets march up the hole to a sense node at the top. With only four phase lines, the staircase and per-tier contacts disappear.
why: Fact 2 and capital: one critical hole mask for ~200 tiers, no staircase (10+ masks and trims in 3D NAND) and no capacitor pillar; shifting at ~2 GHz gives ~50 ns average latency, and recirculation doubles as refresh. Risk is charge-transfer efficiency and dark current in a deposited channel liner.
note: One hole mask for 200 tiers, no staircase or capacitor; charge-transfer efficiency and dark current in deposited liners are the doubt.

title: Vertical plated-wire memory: NiFe-lined holes through word-plane stack
idea: Revive 1960s plated-wire memory (NiFe electroplated on beryllium-copper wire, non-destructive readout, flown in Apollo-era and Skylab systems): etch vertical holes through an epitaxial stack of heavily doped silicon word planes by metal-assisted chemical etching, electroplate a circumferentially magnetized NiFe film on each hole wall around a copper core, and store a bit where each word plane crosses a hole. A word current tilts the magnetization slightly and the core senses the induced voltage without destroying it.
why: Facts 2 and 8: a 3D array from one critical hole mask using only aqueous etch and plating (no rare gas), with readout that avoids destructive read and writeback. Risks are mV-level read signal below 100 nm and word-plane selectivity.
note: 3D NDRO magnetic memory from one hole mask is new; inductive read signal collapses at sub-100 nm.

title: Core-rope weights: maskless via-programmed BEOL ROM frees HBM
idea: Revive Apollo's core-rope memory, where the wiring itself encoded the program: build generic base wafers with 8 stacked metal crossbar levels and encode a frozen model's weights only in the via layers, written maskless by multibeam e-beam, so each model ships as a ROM chiplet. Weights leave DRAM; HBM keeps only activations and KV cache.
why: Doing DRAM's job with less: static weights are ~50-80% of inference memory; 4F2 per via level x 8 levels at 40 nm metal pitch is ~DRAM-class density with no capacitor, no refresh and no per-model mask set.
